header.description: What: a parked vehicle heated by the sun is seen by thermal against cool grass (CE-1987, R-1058; docs/DESIGN_Thermal_And_Acoustic_Sensing.md §9.2, §9.7). On wide-corridor — a street whose roadway is a 30 m GRASS strip (y 185–215, x 60–540) between houses and hedges — at 13:36 local (solar ~12:30), clear sky: 'Observer' (the thermal observer, TKB 215: a hand-held sight that needs 4 K of contrast) stands on the strip at (70, 200); 'Grass Tank', a T-72 parked with its engine OFF, stands on the strip at (420, 200), 350 m along the street. Judge: the hull is at the sun-heated painted-metal °C, many K above the grass, so the observer's memory holds it with the THERMAL bit (4) — the old rule never saw a cold-engined hull (0.2 < 0.3). His eyes may also see it (daylight): only the thermal bit is judged. Fail: no thermal bit. Red-proof: the field read as bare soil (Open surfaces not stamped in the surface grid) and the hull stays within 4 K. Its sibling th-hull-on-hot-soil holds the other half.
